context: Read-only design analysis (subagent): merged routing proposals 2+3 with read-audit S1-F into one W3/2.18.0 store-identity design (resolution trace on status, ancestor/out-of-repo warning, expect_project on assemble, store_id stamped in config.yml, toolResult store echo). Key discovered fact: the SERVER has no ancestor walk — resolveProjectRoot (src/utils/project-root.ts:66-92) is argv>env>worktree-redirect>cwd only; the ancestor walk exists solely in the five hook copies (activity-marker-hook.sh else-branch), whose comment claims it 'matches the server's resolution' but does not — hooks walk past cwd into ancestor stores the server would never bind, and the server silently CREATES cwd/.twining where hooks would bind an ancestor (split-brain risk). Also: live store config.yml has project_name '.' (from --project . verbatim passthrough) — concrete proof of basename-identity ambiguity that store_id fixes. No code changed.
rationale: the server cannot observe hook-side binds, and changing binding semantics is the field's own flagged breaking change; warn-first matches proposal 2's explicit non-breaking ask.
summary: Chose to scope the merged routing design to server-side detection only (trace + warnings + expect_project + store_id), leaving hook-walk/server divergence as a documented residual and Issue 1's relative-TWINING_PROJECT semantics change out
